title: Security posture discovery - Halcyon Financial
next_steps: Send SOC 2 Type II report and ISO attestation PDF
Share Private/VPC deployment checklist and network diagram template
Schedule technical deep dive for Dedicated perf benchmarking with Daniel and Marco (next week)
Provide draft contract language for data residency & KMS integration
action_items: Aisha - email SOC2 + ISO docs by 2026-03-22
Marco - prepare Dedicated benchmark plan and sample config by 2026-03-25
Sophie - share Halcyon's data retention policy and regulatory requirements by 2026-03-24
summary: Discovery focused on security posture and deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). Customer primary concerns: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML and RBAC integration, audit logs and CloudTrail parity, encryption/KMS keys for both data at rest and in transit, and data residency/retention controls. Agreed next steps to share compliance artifacts, schedule technical bench for Dedicated, and provide contract language around KMS and retention.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-20 15:00 UTC | Duration: 47m | Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Hannah Lee (Redwood CSM); Sophie Tan (CISO, Halcyon), Liam O'Connor (Head of Cloud Ops), Priya Mehta (Legal), Daniel Kim (SRE)

[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick intros — I'm Aisha, I'm the account exec for Halcyon.
[00:08] Sophie: Hi, Sophie here, CISO at Halcyon. We'll be focused on security and compliance.
[00:12] Liam: Liam O'Connor, cloud ops. We'll be doing the infra review.
[00:15] Priya: Priya, legal — I'll be looking at contract and data residency stuff.
[00:19] Marco: Marco Ruiz, solutions engineer on Redwood, I'll do the technical bits.
[00:23] Daniel: Daniel Kim, SRE, hi.

[00:30] Aisha: Great, agenda—quick 10 minute overview from us, then deep dive on security posture: SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, and data retention. Then we'll capture next steps. Sound good?
[00:42] Sophie: Yep, sounds good.

[01:05] Marco: Okay, really quick on Redwood: we provide Hosted API, Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools), and Private — which is the VPC/on-prem option. Our security stack shifts a bit depending on deployment. Hosted has SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 attestation, and per-tenant logical separation; Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and VPC peering options; Private is customer-managed network and optional on-prem package.
[01:35] Sophie: Quick question — for SOC2, do you have an attestation we can share with our auditors? And is it Type II?
[01:40] Aisha: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II reports and ISO 27001. I'll send the PDFs after this call.
[01:46] Sophie: Great. Also need to understand scope — does Hosted include backup systems and logging in scope?

[02:10] Marco: For Hosted, the SOC2 scope covers the control plane and our managed storage for model artifacts and logs. We redact PII in telemetry, and we have retention controls — though for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private. There can be confusion — sorry if I say Redwood Dedicated or Red wood Dedicate, my bad, but basically Dedicated isolates compute for you.

[02:40] Liam: On Dedicated, how does networking work? We want VPC peering, private links, and minimal internet egress. Also, can we host in our cloud account?

[03:00] Marco: Dedicated supports VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink for hosted regions; we can also provision a Dedicated cluster within your cloud account in some cases — that's more like a Private offering. For the standard Dedicated, networking is configured with customer VPC peering and routes, and you can lock down egress via security groups.

[03:30] Sophie: Encryption: at-rest keys — do you use customer-managed keys (CMK) in KMS? We need to be able to control key rotation and key revocation.

[03:45] Marco: Good question. For Hosted we encrypt at rest with keys we manage by default, but we do offer an option for customer-managed keys via AWS KMS in many regions — we call that KMS BYO (bring your own). For Dedicated/Private you can have KMS integration where the CMK is in your account for the Dedicated-in-customer-account or in your HSM. Not all regions have full parity yet — we'll include region specifics in the doc I send.

[04:20] Sophie: And for in-transit? TLS mutual auth?

[04:24] Marco: TLS 1.2/1.3 for all traffic, and you can enforce mTLS for Private deployments. For Hosted we do client certs for internal services; external API uses standard TLS with strict ciphers. We also support IP allowlists and network ACLs on Dedicated.

[04:45] Priya: From legal perspective — data retention and deletion. If we request deletion of customer data, what's the SLA and what data types are deletable? Also, do you retain model inputs/outputs?

[05:00] Marco: By default, Hosted retains logs and telemetry for X days (I think 90 by default, configurable) — I might be off on the exact number, I'll confirm. For PII or regulated data, we can set retention to meet your policy. For Dedicated/Private we can configure zero retention for user input logs in many setups. We do have a model artifact retention separate from request logs. We'll share the retention matrix.

[05:30] Sophie: Important: auditors will ask whether customer data is used to train models.

[05:36] Aisha: We do not use customer-provided prompt inputs to train our base models for Hosted — there's an option to opt-in to usage for improvements, but it's off by default. We'll include that in the documentation.

[05:50] Daniel: Auditability — do you provide immutable audit logs? Can we ship logs into our CloudTrail or Splunk?

[05:58] Marco: Yes, we export audit logs and request logs. For Dedicated we can push logs to your S3 bucket or CloudWatch; we can forward audit events to your SIEM via secure delivery. For Hosted we provide an audit log export that you can pull; for Private it's in your environment so you control ingestion. There are some naming inconsistencies in our examples, sometimes it shows up as KV cache ops or K V cash ops due to transcriptions in older docs, sorry — but the actual events are detailed.

[06:35] Sophie: RBAC — need SCIM + SSO/SAML integration. We have strict role separation: security admins, devs, ops, compliance. Can you do SCIM provisioning?

[06:48] Marco: Yes, Hosted supports SSO via SAML and SCIM provisioning (provision/deprovision). For Dedicated we can integrate with your IdP directly via SAML/SCIM. For Private deployments, you manage the IdP connector. RBAC roles are customizable: we have built-in roles and you can create custom roles scoped to routes and models.

[07:15] Sophie: Is there a separation between who can access logs vs who can call inference endpoints?

[07:21] Marco: Yes, separate permissions. We use token-based access for API calls and RBAC for console/log access. Tokens can be scoped to routes/model and you can rotate them.

[07:35] Liam: Regulatory/data residency — we operate in EU and APAC and need data to stay within region. Hosted has regions — can you guarantee that data stays in-region?

[07:46] Marco: We support region-specific deployments. For strict guarantees, Dedicated or Private is the recommended path because Hosted can have cross-region backups for durability unless explicitly contracted otherwise. We'll include data residency guarantees for Dedicated contract language.

[08:10] Priya: Contractually we need right to audit and penetration testing windows. Does Redwood allow customer audits or penetration testing for Dedicated/Private?

[08:21] Aisha: For Dedicated and Private, we can negotiate right-to-audit clauses; for Hosted we provide third-party attestations (SOC2, ISO) and pen test summaries. Direct audits on the hosted control plane are generally not allowed, but we can provide evidence and coordinate with our security team.

[08:40] Sophie: How about secrets management — where do you store API tokens and any secret material?

[08:46] Marco: Secrets are stored encrypted at rest, with KMS-managed keys. For Hosted keys are in our cloud account unless you provide CMKs. For Dedicated/Private they can live in your KMS/HSM. Access to secrets is tightly controlled and audited.

[09:10] Daniel: For the Dedicated benchmarking — we want to run some tail-latency scenarios with long context windows and kv-cache warmups. Can we run a perf test?

[09:20] Marco: Absolutely. We typically run a benchmark plan that includes request distribution, sequence lengths, caching warmup, and failure scenarios. We'll need sample prompts and target p95/p99 numbers. We'll set up a short dedicated cluster for a perf run or run inside your Dedicated instance depending on the procurement trajectory.

[09:40] Sophie: One more — audit logs retention and tamper-proofing. Do you provide WORM-like storage or signed log chains?

[09:50] Marco: For Hosted we provide append-only audit logs with integrity checks and can export to your S3 with Object Lock for WORM policies. For Dedicated/Private you can enable S3 Object Lock semantics in your account. We'll explain the options in the docs.

[10:15] Priya: Regarding SSO/SAML, we require SAML2.0 and SCIM 2.0 — any gotchas?

[10:22] Marco: We support SAML 2.0 and SCIM 2.0. Gotchas: provisioning delays, attribute mappings (email vs userPrincipalName), and some IdPs require specific assertion attributes for groups. We'll include a mapping template.

[10:40] Aisha: I'd like to cover an example compliance ask: customer wants logs forwarded to their SIEM, CMKs, region-only data storage, and contractual right to audit. That would typically push them toward Dedicated or Private — does that align with your assessment?

[10:55] Sophie: Yes, sounds right. We prefer Dedicated if procurement timeline allows — cheaper than full on-prem but gives control.

[11:05] Liam: Timeline question — procurement wants a 3-month pilot, then go full production in 90 days after pilot. Is that feasible?

[11:12] Aisha: It's common. We can do a 90-day pilot on Dedicated with commit-to-convert options. The tricky part is KMS/HSM integration and legal review, but those are usually handled in parallel.

[11:26] Marco: For the pilot we'll propose a config: Dedicated cluster with VPC peering, CMK in customer account, log forwarding to customer's S3/CloudWatch, and a limited retention policy aligned with compliance. We'll lay out steps and timings in the benchmarking plan.

[11:45] Sophie: On data use — please put in writing that Hosted won't use our prompts to train models by default.

[11:53] Aisha: Yes, we'll include that in the security docs and in the contract addendum.

[12:05] Daniel: Any known feature gaps — e.g., field-level encryption or tokenization at the service level?

[12:12] Marco: We don't do field-level encryption for arbitrary payloads at the service layer by default, though you can do application-side tokenization or client-side encryption before sending to the API. For Private we can integrate a sidecar-encryption layer. We'll flag it as an architecture pattern.

[12:35] Priya: For legal we want sample contract language around data residency, KMS controls, and right to audit.

[12:42] Aisha: We'll include draft clauses and an outline of our standard security appendix.

[13:00] Sophie: For the SOC2 report, do you have any exceptions or open findings in the last year?

[13:06] Aisha: No open critical findings. The SOC2 report includes a management response section. I'll attach the report and a one-page summary.

[13:20] Marco: Quick note — sometimes in our internal examples we call KV cache "K V cash" in auto transcripts; ignore typos. The technical audit will show exact event names like kv_cache_hit, kv_cache_miss, etc.

[13:40] Liam: Are there rate limits and quotas that we need to be aware of in Dedicated? We want burst capacity for business hours.

[13:48] Marco: Dedicated supports autoscaling and burst pools. We provide quota controls and can set guarantees per-customer. We'll propose an SLA for latency and throughput in the Dedicated contract.

[14:05] Priya: Anything else on e-discovery or legal hold?

[14:10] Marco: For Dedicated/Private you control object retention and legal hold via your S3/Object Lock. For Hosted we can apply retention flags within the log export pipeline.

[14:30] Aisha: OK let's recap next steps — I'll send SOC2/ISO docs; Marco will send benchmark plan and Dedicated config; Sophie will share Halcyon's retention policy and regulatory mappings; we'll schedule the technical deep dive for next week. Anything to add?

[14:45] Sophie: That covers it. Thanks.

[14:50] Aisha: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials and a calendar invite for the deep dive. Bye.

End of transcript.
